title: Starting this fall, you’ll be able to take a Pokémon Jet flight to Japan
description: ANA announces new international routes for its Pokémon Jet collaboration. Earlier this summer, Japanese airline ANA started flying a Pokémon Jet, carrying passengers in an aircraft with awesome and adorable Pocket Monster graphics both inside and out. All of the flights were for domestic routes, primarily linking Tokyo’s Haneda and Osaka’s Itami with regional airports. […]
content:
ANA announces new international routes for its Pokémon Jet collaboration.

Earlier this summer, Japanese airline ANA started flying a Pokémon Jet, carrying passengers in an aircraft with awesome and adorable Pocket Monster graphics both inside and out. All of the flights were for domestic routes, primarily linking Tokyo’s Haneda and Osaka’s Itami with regional airports.

But while it may have started in Japan, Pokémon is one of the most popular entertainment franchises in the whole world, with a fanbase that now stretches far beyond its home country, and that fanbase will be happy to know that starting next month, you’ll be able to fly to or from Japan on a Poké-plane, as ANA is adding international Pokémon Jet routes.

Much like the connected Pokémon video games get their own subtitles, this new themed ANA aircraft is called the Pokémon Jet Green, and accompanying passengers on their flight will be each and every generation’s Grass-type starters, up to and including the representative for the yet-to-be-released Pokémon Winds and Waves. Oh, and of course Pikachu will be there too.

▼ Bulbasaur, Sprigatito, Chespin, Snivy, and Browt

▼ Turtwig, Treecko, Rowlet, Grookey, and Chikorita

As for where this crew will be flying, the Pokémon Jet Green will connect Japan with the U.S., Canada, Australia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, India, Indonesia, and Malaysia. All flights will arrive at or depart from either Haneda Airport in Tokyo or Narita Airport, located in Chiba Prefecture but also servicing the greater Tokyo area.

● Routes to/from Haneda and Honolulu, Seattle, Vancouver, Sydney, Manilla, Singapore, Delhi, Bangkok, Jakarta, and Kuala Lumpur
● Routes to/from Narita and Perth, Singapore, Bangkok, Jakarta, and Mumbai

▼ Pokémon Jet Green routes

In addition to the exterior artwork for the Bowing 787-9, there’ll be Pokémon theming going on inside the cabin as well, with special Pokémon Jet Green designs for the passenger seat headrest covers as well as the napkins and cups used for drink service.

ANA is also promising the presence of Pokémon background music, though it’s not clear if that means familiar tunes will play during boarding or whether a selection will be available for listening through the in-flight entertainment system. We do know, however, that passengers will receive an exclusive Pokémon Jet Green sticker to commemorate their flight.

The Pokémon Jet Green will make its maiden flight on September 18, departing from Haneda at 9:55 p.m. and headed for Honolulu, and will fly back to Haneda at 1:55 p.m., also on September 18 (yes, flying across the international date line is weird). Subsequent schedules are yet to be announced, but ANA says the Pokémon Jet Green will be soaring around the Pacific Rim through March 27 of next year.

content:
New drinks showcase the delicious taste and texture of cold potatoes.


As summer slowly eases its grip on the country and makes way for autumn, Starbucks Japan is welcoming the change of seasons with a classic autumnal ingredient: sweet potato.

There will be two new drinks showcasing the tuber: the Torori Mitsuimo Beni Haruka Frappuccino (from 687 yen [US$4.30]) and the Torori Mitsuimo Beni Haruka Mousse Tea Latte (from 628 yen). As the names suggest, the type of sweet potato used is the Beni Haruka, a popular variety in Japan, with a focus on “mitsuimo” (literally “honey potato”), the term used to describe sweet potatoes whose natural sugars become concentrated into a honey-like sweetness when baked.

The soft and gooey mitsuimo texture is said to be replicated beautifully in both drinks, through a sweet potato paste made from Japanese Beni Haruka. In the Frappuccino, the paste is combined with milk to create a rich sweetness, with roasted sweet potato-flavoured sauce drizzled over the whipped cream for an enticing roasted aroma. To finish, the drink is topped with roasted sweet potato-flavoured chips, inspired by “imomitsu” (“potato honey”), the caramelised, honey-like juices that ooze out and harden on the surface of a sweet potato as it bakes.

The Torori Mitsuimo Beni Haruka Mousse Tea Latte pairs the chilled Beni Haruka sweet potato paste with a milk tea blend featuring Darjeeling and Assam. On top sits a fluffy sweet potato-flavoured mousse, which can be enjoyed on its own at first, before being mixed into the milk tea for added depth of flavour.

While sweet potatoes are traditionally enjoyed hot and freshly baked, Starbucks says it wanted to highlight how the texture and taste change when chilled. Rather than being soft and fluffy, a chilled sweet potato can become moist and creamy, bringing out a different side to its sweetness.

▼ Rounding out the sweet potato offerings is the Beni Haruka and Annoimo Baked Mitsuimo Cake.

This cake combines two varieties of Japanese sweet potato: Beni Haruka, known for its refined sweetness, and Annoimo, which has a richer, more honey-like flavour. The combination is designed to balance the lighter sweetness of Beni Haruka with the deeper richness of Annoimo, and can be enjoyed hot or cold. When hot, the cake has a roasted aroma, with a gooey, honey-like sweetness and caramelised surface, and when chilled, it has a dense, smooth texture and concentrated sweetness.

All the items in the new release are a great way to get a taste of a very Japanese seasonal flavour, and they’ll be available at Starbucks stores across Japan for a limited time from 2 September.
